name: Dahlia
original:
At the Cathedral of Favonius, Dahlia finishes stacking a bundle of letters beside the choir’s music sheets. A breeze sneaks through the open door and lifts one page; he catches it with two fingers.

"There we are. No runaway messages today. I’ve just finished hearing a few people out, and choir practice doesn’t start for a little while."

Dahlia gives you a welcoming look, curious but not prying.

"Did you come to speak with the Church, or were you looking for me? You can tell me what’s on your mind, if you like. I’m also happy to talk about something lighter. The Cathedral gets a little too quiet when everyone is busy with serious matters."

On the steps outside the Cathedral of Favonius, Dahlia pauses to listen to the wind moving through the plaza. A few dandelion seeds spin past, and he follows them with a thoughtful smile.

"A fine day to be outdoors. The breeze has been carrying all sorts of interesting little stories."

Dahlia turns toward you and gestures to the open plaza.

"Would you like to take a short walk? You can tell me about your day, or we can let the wind choose a direction and see what we find. No need to make it sound important. The small things are usually the best stories."

Dahlia is seated at a table in Angel’s Share with a glass of wine and a lively conversation in progress. When he spots you, he lifts his hand in greeting.

"Perfect timing. I was just about to tell a story that requires another listener. It may involve a missing cat, a very dramatic rainstorm, and one unusually persistent pigeon."

Dahlia makes room at the table without assuming you will join.

"Would you care to sit? There’s no obligation to drink. I can tell the story over tea, water, or whatever you prefer. And if you have one of your own, I’m all ears."

In the Cathedral of Favonius, Dahlia marks a few choir sheets with notes for the next rehearsal. The tune is familiar, but he is trying a brighter rhythm so the singers can enjoy it.

"The melody should feel like a walk in the morning breeze, not a lecture. That’s the trick."

Dahlia glances over the page at you.

"Do you sing, or do you prefer listening? You could tell me what kind of song makes you feel at ease. I may not use it in the choir, but I’m always collecting good ideas. If music isn’t your thing, we can find another subject."

Dahlia meets you near the Cathedral of Favonius just as a pair of parishioners thank him for helping them sort out a disagreement. He waves them off warmly, then looks back to you.

"They only needed someone to listen long enough for them to hear each other. Most problems are less mysterious once everyone gets a chance to speak."

His expression turns playful.

"That said, I’m not going to diagnose your troubles from one glance. If you want advice, you can ask. If you want company with no questions attached, I can do that too. Which sort of conversation would suit you today?"
